name: Amazon seller suspension Plan of Action drafting (simple categories)
buyer: Small Amazon third-party sellers whose accounts are suspended or deactivated and who cannot sell while the appeal is pending
pain: Sellers need a Plan of Action with root cause, corrective actions and preventive measures. Thin or generic appeals fail and repeated thin submissions can slow the process.
wedge: A $495 flat offer for one simple category, such as account-health or performance notices, plus a $99 Plan of Action review. The researcher rates this weak for a no-credibility entrant.

scan1Edge.entrant_basis: A narrow single-category scope with templated drafting using AI tools lets a solo founder charge $495 flat.
scan1Edge.falsifier: If sellers refuse an unknown, anonymous provider at any price, or the cheap tier attracts only unrecoverable cases, the price edge does not convert to revenue.

unitEconomicsNoted.notes: The researcher estimates 70-85% margin per case, but revenue is lumpy and trust is a barrier. No measured variable cost.

majorUncertainty: Trust: an anonymous entrant with no track record must persuade sellers with frozen revenue to pay, and the cheap tier may attract the least recoverable cases.
unknowns: Success rate on simple categories for a new entrant
The Amazon Global Appeals price (the page is old and the excerpt omits the figure)
regulatoryOrPlatformDependency: Depends on Amazon's rules and appeal channels, which change. Some competitors are attorney-run and legal-sounding work by a non-lawyer could raise unauthorized-practice-of-law concerns (not researched).
